description: 20 AI-authored scenarios frozen before inference as an additional evaluation set distinct from gameplay-v1 and heldout-v1. Rubrics and outcomes require independent human Magic judge review; this run is exploratory until then.

messages.content: I cast a creature spell using its bestow cost, targeting my opponent’s creature. In response, that creature leaves the battlefield. Does my spell go to the graveyard or can it still resolve?

cases.expected_answer: It can still resolve as a creature spell; it stops being bestowed when its target is illegal.

criteria.description: Says it can resolve as a creature spell.
Explains the illegal target ends the bestowed/Aura mode rather than countering the spell.

messages.content: I cast a mutating creature spell targeting a creature. Before it resolves, the target is removed. Is the mutating spell countered by the game, or does it resolve in another way?

cases.expected_answer: It continues resolving as a creature spell and enters the battlefield normally.

criteria.description: Says the spell continues resolving as a creature spell.
Says it enters under its controller’s control.

messages.content: My Saga has just triggered its final chapter ability, which is still on the stack. Is the Saga sacrificed immediately because it has enough lore counters?

cases.expected_answer: No. It is not sacrificed while it is the source of a chapter ability still on the stack; the state-based action can apply after that ability leaves the stack.

criteria.description: Says it is not sacrificed while its chapter ability remains on the stack.
Identifies this as a state-based action that does not use the stack.

messages.content: I cast an artifact creature as a 2/2 prototype, then it dies. In my graveyard, does it still have prototype power/toughness, or its normal characteristics?

cases.expected_answer: It has only its normal characteristics in the graveyard; prototype values apply on the battlefield and stack only when cast as prototyped.

criteria.description: Says a prototype card in the graveyard has only normal characteristics.
Distinguishes its prototyped characteristics while on stack/battlefield from other zones.

messages.content: A spell says “deal 2 damage to target creature.” I cast it using overload, which changes “target” to “each.” Does it affect an opponent’s creature with hexproof?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. The overloaded spell does not require targets and may affect objects that could not have been chosen as legal targets, including a hexproof creature.

criteria.description: Says overload changes target wording to each.
Says the overloaded spell can affect a hexproof object because it does not target.

messages.content: My leveler already has the maximum number of level counters shown on its card. Can I activate its level up ability again if I can pay?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. A leveler’s level up ability is present at all times and may be activated regardless of its current number of level counters.

criteria.description: Says level up can still be activated at any level.
Explains the ability adds a level counter and is sorcery-speed.

messages.content: An effect puts a flying keyword counter on my creature. Does that counter give the creature flying, or is it only a marker?

cases.expected_answer: It gives the creature flying. A keyword counter causes that object to gain the keyword.

criteria.description: Says the creature gains flying from the keyword counter.

messages.content: I cast the Adventure half of a card and it resolves. The card is exiled instead of going to the graveyard. Can I later cast its creature half from exile, and can I cast the Adventure half again using that permission?

cases.expected_answer: While it remains exiled, you may play the card, including its creature half. That permission does not let you cast it as an Adventure again.

criteria.description: Says the resolving Adventure spell is exiled and may later be played while it remains there.
Says that permission cannot cast it as an Adventure.

messages.content: I foretell a card during my turn. Can I cast it later in that same turn by paying its foretell cost?

cases.expected_answer: No. The foretell permission allows casting only after the current turn has ended.

criteria.description: Says it cannot be cast during the turn it was foretold.
Says it may be cast after that turn by paying the foretell cost.

messages.content: The last time counter is removed from my suspended card during upkeep. Must I cast it, and do I pay its mana cost?

cases.expected_answer: Casting is optional. If you choose to play it, you may do so without paying its mana cost if able; otherwise it remains exiled.

criteria.description: Says casting is optional when the last time counter is removed.
Says it may be played without paying its mana cost if able, otherwise remains exiled.

messages.content: My opponent has an instant on the stack. I have priority and control a face-down creature with morph. May I pay its morph cost and turn it face up now, and does that use the stack?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Turning it face up this way is a special action available while you have priority and it does not use the stack.

criteria.description: Says it can be turned face up while its controller has priority.
Says this is a special action that does not use the stack.

messages.content: A double-faced card is returned directly from my graveyard to the battlefield by an effect. No instruction specifies a face. Which face enters?

cases.expected_answer: It enters with its front face up by default.

criteria.description: Says the front face enters up by default when put onto the battlefield from a non-stack zone.

messages.content: A creature with afterlife 2 is exiled directly from the battlefield instead of dying. Do I create two Spirit tokens?

cases.expected_answer: No. Afterlife triggers only when the permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield; exile does not satisfy that event.

criteria.description: Says afterlife triggers on a battlefield-to-graveyard event.
Says direct exile does not create the tokens.

messages.content: I just gained control of a creature without haste this turn. May I tap it to pay another attacker’s enlist cost as it attacks?

cases.expected_answer: No. Enlist can tap a creature that has haste or has been under your control continuously since the turn began; this creature meets neither condition.

criteria.description: Says enlist has the haste/continuous-control requirement for the creature tapped.
Connects enlist to an optional cost to attack and its power bonus.

messages.content: My 4/4 with mentor attacks alongside my 3/3. Can the mentor ability target that 3/3?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. The 3/3 is an attacking creature with power less than the 4/4, so it is a legal target for the mentor trigger.

criteria.description: Says mentor triggers when the creature attacks and can target a smaller-power attacking creature.

messages.content: I cast a creature this turn and it has no haste. May I tap it to help pay the convoke cost of another spell?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Convoke lets you tap an untapped creature you control to pay mana; summoning sickness does not prohibit tapping it for another spell’s cost.

criteria.description: Says convoke can tap an untapped creature to pay the spell’s cost.
Distinguishes convoke from activating the creature’s own tap-symbol ability or attacking.

messages.content: I cast a spell with casualty 2 and sacrifice a 2/2 as its additional cost. Does the spell get copied, and may the copy have a different target?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Paying casualty’s sacrifice cost causes its cast trigger to copy the spell, and if it has targets you may choose new ones for the copy.

criteria.description: Says sacrificing a creature with power at least 2 is the casualty cost.
Says paying it creates a copy and permits new targets.

messages.content: Myriad creates two attacking token copies in a four-player game. What happens to those tokens at end of combat?

cases.expected_answer: They are exiled at end of combat. Myriad creates tapped-and-attacking copies for the other opponents, then exiles the tokens at end of combat.

criteria.description: Says myriad creates tapped and attacking token copies for each other opponent.
Says the tokens are exiled at end of combat.

messages.content: A creature enchanted by an Aura with totem armor would be destroyed by lethal damage. Is the creature destroyed?

cases.expected_answer: No. Totem armor replaces that destruction: remove all damage marked on the creature and destroy the Aura instead.

criteria.description: Says the Aura is destroyed instead of the enchanted permanent.
Says damage is removed from the permanent.

messages.content: An effect tells me to bolster 2. I control two creatures tied for least toughness and one larger creature. How do I choose and place the counters?

cases.expected_answer: Choose one of the creatures tied for least toughness and put both +1/+1 counters on that creature.

criteria.description: Says the chosen creature must have least toughness or be tied for least.
Says all 2 counters are put on the one chosen creature.
